A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Aria and AriaScorer research. Their main text, tables, figures, mathematical examples, and appendices support reliable comparison across additions and relocations.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, expert-validated semantic-checker comparisons, component ablations, and generated-formalization case studies.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds subject-level ProofNet results, failure analysis, and a reported Borel conjecture formalization.

M1.justification: The dependency-graph decomposition, LeanSearch grounding, bottom-up synthesis, compiler reflection, and term-grounded scorer are retained. New prompts and discussion clarify the existing procedure; preliminary semantic-feedback experiments do not replace the proposed architecture.

E1.justification: Appendix E.2 adds a research-level topology scenario through Borel's conjecture. The ProofNet subject breakdown disaggregates existing coverage, and the UFD example revisited in B.5 already appeared in B.1.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in the existing benchmark, checker, and ablation tables is unchanged. Table 6 uses the existing Goedel-V2 baseline. BEq is discussed critically but is not newly evaluated as a comparator.

E3.justification: Appendix B.4.1 newly reports preliminary experiments using intermediate semantic feedback, adding an experimental condition beyond terminal-only checking. Existing benchmark settings, including pass@k budgets, 16 reflection attempts, and the operational scorer threshold of 0.9, remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 substantially broadens supplementary analysis with semantic-feedback observations, error-propagation analysis and a CatenaryRing case, a new equivalence analysis of the existing UFD example, ProofNet subject comparisons, and the Borel case. The original component-ablation tables are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report counts and point estimates without seed information, repeated-run variability, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Describing propagated errors as 'statistically rare' adds no uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Tables 1–5 retain their values. v2 adds Table 6's subject-level scores, a reported single FATE-X error-propagation failure, and the Borel formalization outcome. Appendix C.2 corrects the GoT-ablated FATE-H accuracy from 56% in prose to 54%, matching the unchanged Table 5.

T1.justification: Appendix A.1 adds I.IsTwoSided constraints to the nil-ideal definition and Koethe conjecture hypothesis, changing the displayed formal assumptions. New cases add mathematical definitions and B.5 adds equivalence reasoning. No general correctness theorem or proof for Aria is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the same principal method, novelty, and performance claims. The additional appendix material does not redefine the central contributions.

C2.justification: New discussion addresses terminal versus intermediate checking, instability, computational cost, evaluator bias, shallow dependency graphs, and limitations of syntactic evaluation. Appendix C.2 adds a namespace/typeclass explanation for GoT's compilation costs, while Appendix E discusses cross-domain applicability conditional on library support.

D1.justification: New Appendix D supplies prompt frameworks for decomposition, grounding, definition synthesis, statement synthesis, and reflection. Together with explicit documentation of terminal-only scorer use, this substantially expands implementation information, although some examples and contextual inputs remain placeholders.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds Thakur et al. (2024) and Zhou et al. (2025), alongside an existing Chen et al. citation, to contextualize reflection. Appendix B.5 adds positioning against BEq and syntactic evaluation, without introducing an evaluated baseline.

P1.justification: The main narrative and section order remain stable. Editing concentrates on Appendix C.2, case-study explanations, new appendix subdivisions, and updated affiliations and acknowledgments. The LLM-use declaration moves from Appendix D to F.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table 6 and boxed prompt/code displays, relocates Figure 4 within its case study, and reflows content under a conference header. Existing figures and table structures are otherwise preserved.

improvement.justification: The prompt documentation and corrections improve transparency and precision, but new inconsistencies weaken the added evidence. Table 6 reports Aria compilation rates of 96.7–100% as a ProofNet breakdown, unreconciled with Table 1's 91.6% overall rate. B.5's 95.5% 'alignment' claim is unexplained relative to Table 2's 95.5% precision and 82.6% accuracy. Revised B.3 also identifies the wrong quaternion group while retaining a 'Perfectly match' label. These benefits and harms prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
